issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report

### Affected Package
The issue is caused by package @angular/router


### Is this a regression?
I don't know.


### Description
When we use router with param and this params end with equals sign (=) and there are query params after that, the query params are removed by angular.

Let's take a two links as example:
1.  https://angular-eaf2ld.stackblitz.io/hello/my_name?abc=1
2.  https://angular-eaf2ld.stackblitz.io/hello/my_name=?abc=1

If you go into first link, you will see that link doesn't change and the hello component wrote "my_name". 

If you go into second link, you will see that link has been rewritten to https://angular-eaf2ld.stackblitz.io/hello/my_name so component still wrote "my_name" instead of "my_name=" and removes all query params.

The problem is really important, because we have a Backend API that we can not change in any way, and backend send email to client with link to frontend, where they pass TOKEN that often ends with = and few query params. So, token is invalid, and query params are missed.


## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction
Edit panel: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-eaf2ld

As you can see, I used latest verion of Angular (8.1.2).

Having run into this issue, I investigated the validity of this syntax following a comment in the equivalent issue [31649](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/31649#issuecomment-513484106), specifically whether the equals sign should be percent-encoded. Following the IETF [RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986) on the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax, the equals sign is a [reserved character](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-2.2). However, these characters may or may not be, "defined as delimiters by the generic syntax, by each scheme-specific syntax, or by the implementation-specific syntax of a URI's dereferencing algorithm [...] If a reserved character is found in a URI component and no delimiting role is known for that character, then it must be interpreted as representing the data octet corresponding to that character's encoding in US-ASCII." [Section 3.3](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-3.3) defines the forward slash "/" as the delimiter for the path component. It also states that reserved characters are often used in segments, "to delimit scheme-specific or dereference-handler-specific subcomponents.  For example, the semicolon (";") and equals ("=") reserved characters are often used to delimit parameters and parameter values applicable to that segment." I'm not sure if that implies equal signs can be reserved, because the HTTP scheme does not and its delimiting role is relative to the segment not the path. In either case though, reserved or data, a percent-decoded equals sign seems valid in the path component as per RFC 3986.

According to the [BNF grammar for HTTP URLs in the URL RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1738#section-5), most reserved characters, including `=` but excluding `?`, are in fact allowed in URL path segments:

```
httpurl        = "http://" hostport [ "/" hpath [ "?" search ]]
hpath          = hsegment *[ "/" hsegment ]
hsegment       = *[ uchar | ";" | ":" | "@" | "&" | "=" ]
```

The same is true in the [URI RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#appendix-A):

```
   URI           = scheme ":" hier-part [ "?" query ] [ "#" fragment ]

   hier-part     = "//" authority path-abempty
                 / path-absolute
                 / path-rootless
                 / path-empty

   path-abempty  = *( "/" segment )
   path-absolute = "/" [ segment-nz *( "/" segment ) ]
   path-noscheme = segment-nz-nc *( "/" segment )
   path-rootless = segment-nz *( "/" segment )
   path-empty    = 0<pchar>

   segment       = *pchar
   segment-nz    = 1*pchar
   segment-nz-nc = 1*( unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / "@" )
                 ; non-zero-length segment without any colon ":"

   pchar         = unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" / "@"

   sub-delims    = "!" / "$" / "&" / "'" / "(" / ")"
                 / "*" / "+" / "," / ";" / "="
```

(path segments can contain any number of `pchar` which include `sub-delims` including `"="`).

We have also encountered an issue where a route parameter containing `=` (e.g. `/path/to/key=val`) gets redirected to the URL with the `=` and what follows stripped out (`/path/to/key`). We may be able to URL encode the `=` but it seems like a bug in Angular not to accept what is otherwise a valid path segment?
